question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution mentions that, "There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court such salaries as may be determined by the Parliament by law, and until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries are specified in the Second Schedule"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 125**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 125 of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the salaries of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• It stipulates that the salaries of the Judges shall be determined by the Parliament by law.
 
• Until such a provision is made by the Parliament, the salaries are specified in the Second Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• This provision ensures that the financial independence of the judiciary is maintained, which is crucial for upholding the principle of judicial independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 124**

 
 
• Deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Specifies the process of appointment of the Chief Justice and other Judges of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Article 126**
 
 
• Provides for the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice of India.
 
• An Acting Chief Justice is appointed when the office of the Chief Justice is vacant or when the Chief Justice is unable to perform the duties of the office.
 
 
 
• **Article 127**
 
 
• Deals with the appointment of ad hoc Judges in the Supreme Court.
 
• Allows the Chief Justice of India to request retired Judges to sit and act as a Judge of the Supreme Court for a temporary period.
 
 
 
• **Second Schedule of the Constitution**
 
 
• Specifies the emoluments, allowances, and privileges for various constitutional offices including the President, Governors, Judges, etc.
 
• Ensures a structured and transparent approach towards the remuneration of key public officials.
